# Module `asyncs`

async - a multi-threaded executor with stackful-fiber tasks.

This is the real executor that the earlier `tasks` module's fire-and-forget
threads were steps toward. Each async_spawn task runs on its own stack (a
fiber) pinned to one of the pool's worker threads (one scheduler per CPU core),
and a running fiber can suspend cooperatively without blocking its worker:

import async
a = async_spawn(|| -> { async_sleep_ms(40); return 10 })
b = async_spawn(|| -> { async_sleep_ms(5); return 32 })
v1 = async_await(a)   // drives the loop until a completes -> 10
v2 = async_await(b)   // -> 32   (took ~40ms total, not ~45ms)

Suspension points are the suspendable intrinsics: async_yield() (round-robin
fairness), async_sleep_ms(ms) (a timer, not a thread sleep, so other tasks
proceed), and async_await(t) (block until task `t` completes, returning it).
Because the fibers are stackful, a fn() can suspend mid-body simply by calling
these -- no state-machine transform is required.

Lifecycle: tasks stay valid across main-thread awaits, so you can spawn
several and await them in any order. async_run_all() runs whatever is left and
then reclaims every task (handles must not be used afterwards); a leftover-task
atexit hook stops the worker pool and reclaims anything forgotten.

<a id="sym-async_accept"></a>
### `async_accept` · fn

```
async_accept(fd<Int>)<Int> ->
```

Accept a pending connection on a listening socket, suspending until one
arrives. Returns the connected descriptor (>= 0) or -1.

<a id="sym-async_await"></a>
### `async_await` · fn

```
async_await(t<Int>)<Int> ->
```

Block until task `t` completes and return its closure result. From the entry
thread this parks until the worker delivers it; from inside a fiber it suspends
that fiber while the pool continues other work.

<a id="sym-async_connect"></a>
### `async_connect` · fn

```
async_connect(fd<Int>, ip<String>, port<Int>)<Int> ->
```

Non-blocking connect, suspending until established or refused. Returns 0 on
success, -1 on failure (see network::socket_error_code()).

<a id="sym-async_poll"></a>
### `async_poll` · fn

```
async_poll(t<Int>)<Int> ->
```

Non-blocking: the task's result if it is done, else -1.

<a id="sym-async_recv"></a>
### `async_recv` · fn

```
async_recv(fd<Int>, maxlen<Int>)<String> ->
```

Receive up to `maxlen` bytes from `fd` as a fresh String, suspending until
data is readable. Empty on error or EOF.

<a id="sym-async_run_all"></a>
### `async_run_all` · fn

```
async_run_all()<Int> ->
```

Run the pool until no queued work or pending timer remain, then reclaim tasks.

<a id="sym-async_send"></a>
### `async_send` · fn

```
async_send(fd<Int>, data<String>)<Int> ->
```

Send all of `data` on `fd`, suspending until the socket accepts it. Returns
the number of bytes sent (or -1).

<a id="sym-async_sleep_ms"></a>
### `async_sleep_ms` · fn

```
async_sleep_ms(ms<Int>)<Int> ->
```

Cooperative sleep: suspend the current fiber for `ms` on a timer so other loop
work proceeds. Outside a fiber this sleeps the calling thread.

<a id="sym-async_spawn"></a>
### `async_spawn` · fn

```
async_spawn(work<fn() -> Int>)<Int> ->
```

Enqueue `work` (a fn() -> Int) on the worker pool; returns a task handle (>= 1)
or 0 on failure. The pool runs on the next async_await/async_run_all.

<a id="sym-async_yield"></a>
### `async_yield` · fn

```
async_yield()<Int> ->
```

Cooperative yield: suspend the current fiber and reschedule it (a no-op if
called outside a fiber).
